**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic Number** | 1 | | **Symbol** | H | | **Common Isotopes** |
• ¹H (protium) – most abundant (~99.98%)

• ³H (tritium) – rare; radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 yr) | | **Standard Atomic Weight** | 1.00794 u (weighted average including all stable isotopes) | | **Electron Configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First Ionisation Energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) | | **Second Ionisation Energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ/mol) | | **Molecular Formula** | H₂ (most common form under normal conditions) | | **Bond Dissociation Energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ/mol | | **Boiling Point (at 1 atm)** | −252.87 °C (≈21 K) | | **Melting Point (at 1 atm)** | −259.14 °C (≈14 K) | | **Density at Standard Conditions (STP)** | 0.08988 g/L (for dihydrogen gas) | | **Specific Heat Capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 28.84 J/(mol·K) | | **Heat of Formation (ΔfH°)** | 0 kcal/mol (by definition for elemental state) | | **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as an acid when bonded to more electronegative atoms (e.g., HF); forms hydrides (metallic bonds) with metals; behaves as a weak base in aqueous solution (forming [H₃O]⁺). | | **Oxidation States** | +1 (in acids such as HCl, HBr, HI), -1 (as metal hydride ions or in compounds like LiH, NaBH₄ where it acts as hydride donor). | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive due to low bond strength; readily reacts with halogens, oxygen, nitrogen oxides, and many transition metals. Forms covalent bonds easily; participates in radical chain reactions. | | **Spectroscopic Features** | Strong absorption/emission lines in UV-visible region (Balmer series). Infrared active vibrational mode around 4400 cm⁻¹ for H₂. | ### Additional Notes * **Isotope Effects:** Deuterium and tritium have slightly higher mass leading to lower zero-point energies; this affects reaction kinetics (“kinetic isotope effect”) and spectroscopic frequencies (vibrational frequency ∝ √(μ)). * **Physical State Under Normal Conditions:** Di­molecule H₂ is a colorless, odorless, nonpolar gas. It has very high diffusibility and extremely low viscosity. * **Role in Chemistry & Industry:** Primary source of clean fuel via electrolysis; used in semiconductor manufacturing (etching gases), metallurgy (reducing agent), cryogenics (coolant for superconductors), and as a tracer in nuclear fusion research.
